welcome.heading: Sixteen questions, about eight minutes
welcome.lead: Your answers decide where your programme starts. There is no right answer and nothing to pass — an optimistic answer just gets you a programme that does not fit.
welcome.mirrorBody: Three questions ask you to try a movement and watch what happens. A bathroom mirror in even light is ideal.
welcome.safetyTitle: We will tell you if we are wrong for you
welcome.safetyBody: Some answers mean you need a doctor rather than an app. If that comes up we stop and say so, plainly.
welcome.clinicalNote: These questions were written by our clinical team. The placement they produce follows the same reasoning a physiotherapist uses in a first appointment: time since onset, then what actually moves, then whether movements are linked.

assessment.errRequired: Please answer this one — your programme depends on it.
assessment.errFutureDate: That date is in the future. Please check it.

meta.title: Assessment — Palsya
meta.description: Answer a short questionnaire so we can place you at the right stage of your facial paralysis programme.

phase.blockedLead: Something in your answers needs a doctor rather than a rehabilitation programme. We would rather lose your sign-up than have you start anyway.
phase.blockedSavedBody: Nothing is lost. When you have been seen — or when enough time has passed — sign back in and your assessment will be where you left it. You can also read every guide in the knowledge base in the meantime, free and without an account.
phase.confidenceHigh: High — your answers fit a clear pattern
phase.confidenceLow: Low — a clinician will review this
phase.dailyMeaning: What this means for your day
phase.reviewNotice: A clinician will review this placement. That is because {why}. You can start today — if the review changes anything, you will be told what changed and why, within one working day.
phase.stageNotFixedNote: Your stage is not fixed. It moves when your scans and your own reports say it should — forwards, and sometimes backwards after illness or a heavy stretch of fatigue. Backwards is an adjustment, not lost ground.
phase.confirmText: Only do this if a doctor has assessed you and told you it is appropriate to begin rehabilitation. We will note on your record that you continued past a safety flag.

meta.title: Your stage — Palsya
meta.description: Your programme placement, and why we placed you there.

prefs.heading: How should we fit into your day?
prefs.lead: All of this is changeable later, and none of it is used to nag you.
prefs.remindersBody: One reminder at a time you choose. If you miss it, that is the end of it — there is no second reminder that mentions the first, and nothing that says you have broken anything.
prefs.languageBody: The whole app and every guide, in {count, number} languages. Consultations are with a clinician who speaks yours where possible.
prefs.sizeHint: Many of our users are over 60. This is not buried in a settings menu for a reason.
prefs.mirrorLabel: Mirror the camera preview (most people find this easier)
prefs.weeklySummary: A weekly summary of what was measured and logged
prefs.clinicianUpdates: Tell me when a clinician adds a note or changes my programme

meta.title: Preferences — Palsya
meta.description: Choose reminders, reading size and emails for your programme.

prefs.languageHint: You can change this at any time from the language menu at the top of every page. It does not change anything else about your programme.

consent.heading: What you are agreeing to, in plain words
consent.lead: Two of these are required because the programme cannot function without them. The rest genuinely change nothing about your programme or your price if you decline.

dataProcessing.title: Processing my health data
dataProcessing.body: Your assessment answers, stage, session logs, and notes. This is special category data under GDPR Article 9 and we process it on your explicit consent. Without it there is no programme to run.

photoStorage.title: Analysing scans of my face
photoStorage.body: Landmark detection runs on your device. Storing the images is the next item and is separate — decline that and you still get scores, just no photo timeline.

photoKeep.title: Storing my scan photos so I can see my timeline
photoKeep.body: Kept encrypted, visible only to you and to clinicians you share with. You can delete any single photo, or all of them, at any time, and that deletion is real.

clinicianShare.title: Sharing my progress with a clinician I choose
clinicianShare.body: Only with someone you name, only what you send, and revocable. If you have a referral code from your own physiotherapist, this is the one that lets them see your reports.

researchOptIn.title: Using my anonymised data for research
researchOptIn.body: Aggregated and stripped of identifiers, used to understand what helps. Never sold. Declining changes nothing about your programme, your price, or your clinician.

marketing.title: Occasional emails about new guides and features
marketing.body: Not a newsletter treadmill. Roughly monthly, and unsubscribing takes one click.

consent.laterNote: You can change any of these later, from Settings → Privacy and data. Withdrawing consent for photo storage deletes the stored images; your scores stay unless you delete those separately.
consent.errRequired: The two required consents are needed for the programme to work.

consent.gdprNote: Your health data is special category data under GDPR and is processed only on your explicit consent, encrypted at rest and in transit, and never sold or used for advertising.
consent.termsAgreement: By continuing you agree to Palsya’s <link>Terms of Service and Privacy Policy</link>.
